predecessors.name: Zunbils
predecessors.text: Ghazni, which the Zunbils held on the map to 869

successors.name: Ghaznavid Empire
successors.text: Ghazni and Gardez, taken by Alp-Tegin in 962 and Sabuktigin about 977

ledger.x: 870: the map's Zunbils end at Ghazni; the Lawiks of Ghazni and Gardez take over the map.
962: Alp-Tegin 'wrested the town from its ruler Abu Bakr Lawik' after a four-month siege of the citadel.
c. 965: Abu Bakr Lawik retook Ghazni from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim.
c. 977: Sabuktigin defeated the Lawik and Kabul Shahi alliance near the Logar river; Abu Ali Lawik was killed and Gardez fell about then.
977: Ghaznavid control set up in Ghazni; the dynasty ends.

certainty.note: The page names towns only; no frontier.
